text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Stefan Gavornik, president of the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, said the fund should not continue in direct privatisation sales following a Constitutional Court ruling transferring the resposibility for such deals to the government, even though there still remains some time before the ruling takes effect.
- The Confederation of Trade Unions has warned that it will not sign the 1997 general agreement with the government if parliament ignores its amendments to next year's state budget.

- The largest privatisation fund, Sporofond, will begin to pay to its shareholders 0.40 crowns for a one crown share next week, the fund's administrator Harvard Investment Company said. When forced administration was imposed on the fund in 1994, a one crown share had a value of some 1.54 crowns.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Some 40 percent of industrial companies said they posted increase in production in November, while about 21 percent said they saw a decline. About 31 percent of companies expect production to increase over the next three months. A decline is expected at 10 percent of the firms.
- At present, the private sector accounts for about 70.5 percent of GDP.

- The Slovak Prognostic Bureau said privatisation has so far failed to bring the expected positive results, as some new owners of state property attempt to make personal profit from their ownership rather than for their companies.
- Money market dealers have welcomed the launch of operation of the first local money market broker, MMB Bratislava, saying it could help the market maintain liquidity.

PRAVDA - Jaroslav Paska, a deputy of the junior coalition partner, the Slovak National Party (SNS), said the ruling coalition will probably include a revised version of the controversial law on protection of republic on the agenda of the December session of the parliament.
